passage: Coral polyps can struggle in shallow reef environments because these organisms require enough water flow for nutrient delivery but not so much that they risk structural damage from strong currents. Researchers Sofia Guerrero and Randy Osborne found several colonies of Acropora cervicornis, a type of staghorn coral, growing behind large sea fans in Florida's coral reef system. To evaluate whether these flexible structures benefited the coral, the researchers compared the branch density, a measure of coral growth, of A. cervicornis when growing in open water versus when the coral was growing behind the sea fans. They found that branch density was 58% higher for coral growing behind sea fans as compared to coral in open water, suggesting that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: A. cervicornis growing behind sea fans experience reduced current velocity and are thus able to avoid structural damage.
choices.B: A. cervicornis is one of the few types of coral that can survive behind flexible sea structures.
choices.C: sea fans do not allow the necessary water flow for nutrient delivery in A. cervicornis.
choices.D: sea fans are capable of supporting A. cervicornis growth if the fans are not too dense.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text. The text explains that while coral polyps need sufficient water flow for nutrient delivery, exposure to strong currents can also affect the organisms negatively by causing structural damage. Guerrero and Osborne's team found specimens of A. cervicornis coral growing behind sea fans that were flexible, allowing some but not all water flow to pass through them, and the branch density of these specimens was higher than that of A. cervicornis specimens found growing in open water that were unprotected by such structures. Since, as the text explains, branch density is an indicator of coral growth, and since greater exposure to strong currents results in greater structural damage, it can be inferred that A. cervicornis growing behind sea fans experience reduced current velocity and are thus able to avoid structural damage.
